subject: Clarify cache staleness window and billing triggers for prompt caching
messages:
From: Jacob Lee <jacob@nimblehealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: platform@nimblehealth.com
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 18:02:00 +0000
Subject: Quick Q on cache "staleness window" and when we get charged

Hi Ava —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Two quick follow-ups from our infra team as we scope expected spend:

1) "Staleness window" / TTL: our app uses conversational state that changes frequently. If a cached prefix expires after X minutes, what counts as an expired request vs a charged request? Basically: do you bill when the cache is stale but still returns a partial match?

2) Partial hits and token accounting: if a request hits on the first N tokens from cache but generates M new tokens after, how is billing attributed? Are cached tokens ever billed at all, or do we only pay for the generated tail?

3) Warm-up / onboarding credits: while we ramp, we'll inevitably have a lot of cold requests. Do you offer any transient credits for warm-up traffic or a way to exclude onboarding bursts from the billing baseline?

We want to draft a conservative spend estimate for month 1. Any concrete examples or a short table would help.

Thanks —
Jacob
Platform Eng, NimbleHealth

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Jacob Lee <jacob@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2026 09:17:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick Q on cache "staleness window" and when we get charged

Hi Jacob —

Great questions. Short answers up-front, followed by concrete examples below.

Summary:
- Staleness window (what we call the cache TTL) is configurable per-route; default for hosted customers is 15 minutes. A cache entry older than the TTL is considered expired and will not be treated as a full-hit.
- Billing is determined by the tokens actually produced by the runtime. If the runtime returns an entire response solely from a cached prefix (no new tokens generated server-side), we do not bill generation tokens for that response. If the cache provides a prefix and the model generates additional tokens beyond that prefix, you are billed for the generated tokens only.
- Partial-hit mechanics: the runtime tracks how many tokens were supplied from cache vs generated. We meter and report both counts; only generated tokens are billed at the standard generation rate.
- Warm-up / onboarding: for deals with a committed pilot or enterprise contract we can include a one-time warm-up credit (typically defined in the SOW). For self-serve customers we offer a short free onboarding allowance on request — happy to put numbers on this if you share expected volume.

Examples (assume 100-token prompt + 50-token cached prefix):
- Request A: full-match (cache returns entire 150 tokens) -> billed = 0 generated tokens.
- Request B: cache provides 50-token prefix, model generates remaining 100 tokens -> billed = 100 generated tokens.
- Request C: cache is expired (TTL exceeded) -> full generation for 150 tokens billed.

Behavior notes:
- "Staleness" and partial-match logic are evaluated at request time. If the cached entry is present but older than TTL we treat it as missing for billing and correctness reasons (ensures deterministic behavior).
- We do have a separate metric for "soft hits" (cache returned but flagged stale) so you can see warm-cache efficiency without impacting billing.

I'll attach a condensed matrix that maps request scenarios to billing outcomes. Ben and Laura, looping you in to confirm if we should propose a short warm-up credit in the NimbleHealth pilot and to confirm SOW language.

Cheers,
Ava
Ava Chen

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups:

- Can TTL be set to a per-customer route value? We have some endpoints where staleness tolerance is 2 minutes and others where it's 2 hours.
- For reporting: can you surface the soft-hit metric and separate generated-token charges per route in the Console so we can tie spend back to endpoints?
- For the warm-up credit: what's your typical range (e.g., 100k generated tokens / 30 days) and what level of commit would trigger that?

If you can put those three items into the matrix and confirm what we can expect in the onboarding SOW I'll share with finance.

—Jacob

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jacob Lee <jacob@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick Q on cache "staleness window" and when we get charged

Jacob —

Appreciate the level of detail — good checklist. Quick replies and next steps:

1) TTL per-route: yes. For Hosted API customers we support per-route TTL that we can set at onboarding. We can expose the TTL as a parameter in the route config (Console + API).

2) Reporting: the Console will show three columns per route in the next dashboard release: total requests, soft-hits (cache returned but stale), hard-hits (full cache hit), generated-tokens (billed). We'll share a mock dashboard screenshot in the matrix.

3) Warm-up credit: for pilots tied to a committed 3-month pilot (minimum $10k ARR commitment) standard practice is a one-time onboarding credit that covers up to 200k generated tokens over the first 30 days. If you want a larger allowance we can structure it against a higher commit. We can make the credit specific to generated-token charge only (cached hits remain free per policy above).

Action: Ava & Laura will attach an updated matrix (route examples, TTL settings, billing outcomes) and a one-page SOW paragraph we can propose to Finance. If the matrix looks good we'll fold it into the NimbleHealth pilot SOW (DEAL-9342).

Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
